result.summary: The street environment features a wide roadway with embedded tram tracks and multiple travel lanes, which likely encourages higher vehicle speeds. While continuous sidewalks and mature street trees are present, the lack of marked pedestrian crossings and the significant crossing distance create a challenging environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Embedded Tram Tracks
hazards.description: Steel tracks in the roadway can be a tripping hazard for pedestrians and a significant slip/crash hazard for cyclists.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway extending into the distance

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide, multi-lane roadway lacks any marked crossings or refuge islands, forcing pedestrians to cross a long distance unprotected.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked cars and large tree trunks may obscure pedestrians from the view of oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the curb

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked mid-block crossings with high-visibility continental markings to designate safe crossing points.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at potential crossing points to reduce the crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island between the tram tracks and travel lanes to allow for two-stage crossing.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a residential row-house street with a sidewalk in poor physical condition. A large mature tree and accumulated debris significantly obstruct the walkway, likely forcing pedestrians to navigate uneven surfaces or enter the roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large mature tree trunk occupies nearly the entire width of the paved walkway, forcing pedestrians into the street or onto unpaved ground.

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: The sidewalk is severely cracked, uneven, and degraded, creating significant tripping hazards.

hazards.name: Debris and Trash
hazards.description: Loose trash bags and debris are scattered on the walkway, further reducing usable space.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Repair and level the sidewalk surface to provide a smooth, ADA-compliant path of travel.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening/Bump-outs
interventions.description: Widen the sidewalk or create a curb extension around the tree to maintain a continuous clear walking path without removing the mature vegetation.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians at night.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a narrow sidewalk on the left side, which is partially obstructed by a large mature tree and adjacent parked vehicles. The roadway includes tram tracks and a painted bike lane, but lacks physical separation or buffers between pedestrians and moving traffic.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large tree trunk significantly narrows the effective walking width of the sidewalk, potentially forcing pedestrians closer to the roadway.

hazards.name: Tram Tracks
hazards.description: Embedded tracks in the roadway can be a tripping hazard for pedestrians crossing mid-block and a significant hazard for cyclists.

hazards.name: Lack of Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical buffer or planting strip between the narrow sidewalk and the travel/parking lane, increasing exposure to traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Expand the sidewalk width to accommodate the mature trees while maintaining a clear, accessible walking path.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lane
interventions.description: Convert the painted bike lane into a protected lane using bollards or a raised curb to provide a buffer for both cyclists and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The image depicts a wide, multi-lane commercial arterial road with a car-centric design. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the environment lacks safe crossing infrastructure and features significant visual obstructions from parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A large yellow truck parked at the curb blocks sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the roadway.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide multi-lane roadway requires a long, unprotected crossing for pedestrians with no refuge or marked crosswalk visible.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing with Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk and a raised median refuge island to reduce crossing distance and provide a safe waiting area.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at potential crossing points to increase pedestrian visibility and further shorten the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Warning Beacons
interventions.description: Install Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFBs) to alert motorists to the presence of pedestrians attempting to cross.
